pages.text: The secondary - a long winding and its toroid - rings at its own frequency, 1/2π√(L₂C₂) = 159 kHz. The primary, a capacitor and a few turns, rings at 1/2π√(L₁C₁). Only when the two agree does the energy slosh across to the secondary, where it appears as a voltage higher by √(C₁/C₂). In air an arc reaches about a metre for every 700 kV.
$(thing)Set$(): Primary capacitance, Primary turns tapped, Charging voltage.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Spark-gap jitter: the primary's frequency wanders by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Flashover down the secondary: above 5 MV it arcs along its own winding.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Longer arcs work the charge faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Primary inductance: L₁ ∝ N²$(br)Primary frequency: f₁ = 1/2π√(L₁C₁)$(br)Secondary frequency: f₂ = 1/2π√(L₂C₂)$(br)Detuning: |f₁/f₂ − 1|$(br)Secondary voltage: V₂ = η·V₁·√(C₁/C₂)$(br)Arc length: ℓ ≈ V/(700 kV/m)
